<reflection>
- The first experiment resulted in very similar NLL values for almost all models (around -22), with the exception of M5. This indicates that a standard condition with moderate [S] and [cat] and no [P] is insufficient to break the degeneracy among the models, as most can adjust their rate constants to fit a simple saturation curve.
- The aim of establishing a baseline was achieved, but we now need to probe the non-linear dependencies to separate the models.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
To differentiate the remaining models, we need to introduce conditions that trigger their unique non-linear behaviors. By simultaneously increasing the initial substrate concentration ([S]=2.5), doubling the catalyst concentration ([cat]=0.1), and introducing a high initial product concentration ([P]=0.5), we can probe multiple mechanistic features at once. 
1. The presence of initial product will strongly differentiate models with product-induced deactivation or inhibition (M12, M17, M5) from those without.
2. The higher catalyst concentration will alter the proportion of monomeric vs. dimeric catalyst, testing models with higher-order catalyst dependencies (M2, M3, M13, M18, M19).
3. The increased substrate concentration will test for substrate inhibition or substrate-induced deactivation (M7, M11, M16). 
This combined perturbation will force the models to extrapolate to a new regime, significantly reducing the set of plausible mechanisms by breaking the parameter degeneracy observed in the first run.
</hypothesis>
